page: Amazon Web Services c8g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the ARMv9 arm64 architecture, this instance features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance, with uncached read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 391.61 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 171.76 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. The Geekbench multi-core score of 21,249.0 and Passmark database operations score of 46,834.4 also rank in the top tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations demonstrate strong performance, processing 361.7 GB/sec and 67.77 million operations per second respectively. However, single-core CPU performance and large-model LLM prompt processing show relative weaknesses, with 70B model prompt processing dropping to a weak 5.89 tokens/sec.

The c8g.8xlarge offers a high physical core density and top-tier memory bandwidth relative to its resource profile, making it a cost-efficient option for multi-threaded, memory-bound compute workloads that do not require local storage or GPU acceleration. It is suited for workloads such as database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression. It is less suitable for large-scale LLM inference or workloads requiring high single-core performance.
